 let old=parents.to_owned()+"table children:\n  parent: parents\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
 let parent_fill="backfill parents twice(n: int):\n  {n:n * 2}\n";
 let next=old.replace("  parent: parents","  copied: int\n  parent: parents")+parent_fill+"backfill children copy(parent: parents):\n  {copied:(parents[parent] ! else NOT_FOUND).n}\n";
 let mut e=engine(&old);seed(&mut e,"parents",json!({"id":"p","n":3}));seed(&mut e,"children",json!({"id":"c","parent":"p"}));adopt(&mut e,&next,2).unwrap();
 adopt(&mut e,&(parents.to_owned()+parent_fill),3).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,&next,2).unwrap();
 assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"parents","p","n"),Value::Int(6));assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"children","c","copied"),Value::Int(3));
}

#[test]
fn leaving_the_last_backfill_cannot_remove_an_ended_source_lifetime() {
 let old="table items:\n  n: int\n  until: time\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
 let next=old.replace("  until: time","  until: time\n  expire at .until")+"backfill items twice(n: int):\n  {n:n * 2}\n";
 for absent in [false,true] {
  let(s,p)=compile(old);let mut e=Engine::new_release_prepared_at(Store::memory().unwrap(),s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(1,None),false,0).unwrap();
  let r=wire::row_from_json(&e.schema().tables["items"],&json!({"id":"a","n":3,"until":50})).unwrap();e.seed_at([("items".into(),r)],0).unwrap();
  let(s,p)=compile(&next);e.adopt_release_at(s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(2,Some(1)),false,1).unwrap();
  if absent {let(s,p)=compile("query empty():\n  return true\n");e.adopt_release_at(s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(3,Some(2)),false,2).unwrap();}
  let previous=if absent {3}else{2};let(s,p)=compile(old);e.adopt_release_at(s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(1,Some(previous)),false,100).unwrap();assert_eq!(e.store().count("items").unwrap(),0);
 }
}

}
#[test]
fn saved_reference_inputs_keep_their_own_lifetime_after_live_retargeting() {
 for kind in ["parents","id"] {
 let parents="table parents:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
 let mutation="mutation retarget():\n  update children['c'] {parent:'q'}\n";
 let old=parents.to_owned()+"table children:\n  parent: parents on delete keep\n  public 'fixture'\n  update <- allow\n  online only\n"+mutation;
 let fill=format!("backfill children copy(parent: {kind}):\n  {{copied:(parents[parent] ! else NOT_FOUND).n}}\n");
 let next=old.replace("  parent: parents","  copied: int\n  parent: parents")+&fill;
 let dropped=next.replace("  parent: parents on delete keep\n","").replace(mutation,"");
 let mut e=engine(&old);for(id,n)in[("p",3),("q",9)]{seed(&mut e,"parents",json!({"id":id,"n":n}));}seed(&mut e,"children",json!({"id":"c","parent":"p"}));adopt(&mut e,&next,2).unwrap();write(&mut e,"retarget");adopt(&mut e,&dropped,3).unwrap();
 let table=e.schema().tables["parents"].clone();{let tx=e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();let r=tx.get("parents","p").unwrap().unwrap();tx.delete("parents",&table,&r).unwrap();tx.commit().unwrap();}seed(&mut e,"parents",json!({"id":"p","n":77}));
 adopt(&mut e,parents,4).unwrap();let error=adopt(&mut e,&dropped,3).unwrap_err().to_string();assert!(error.contains("parent lifetime"),"{error}");
}
}

#[test]
fn a_new_reference_output_keeps_its_parent_lifetime_when_the_row_narrows() {
 let old="table parents:\n  name: text <=10\n  unique name\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\ntable children:\n  n: int 0..10\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
 let next=old.replace("  n: int 0..10","  link: parents\n  n: int 0..5")+"backfill children link():\n  {link:(parents[name = 'p'] ! else NOT_FOUND).id}\n";
 let mut e=engine(old);seed(&mut e,"parents",json!({"id":"p","name":"p"}));seed(&mut e,"children",json!({"id":"c","n":9}));adopt(&mut e,&next,2).unwrap();assert_eq!(e.store().count("children").unwrap(),0);
 let table=e.schema().tables["parents"].clone();{let tx=e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();let r=tx.get("parents","p").unwrap().unwrap();tx.delete("parents",&table,&r).unwrap();tx.commit().unwrap();}seed(&mut e,"parents",json!({"id":"p","name":"p"}));
 adopt(&mut e,&next.replace("int 0..5","int 0..10"),3).unwrap();assert_eq!(e.store().count("children").unwrap(),0,"a retained output reference cannot recapture a reused parent");
}

#[test]
fn original_absence_survives_later_defaults_until_a_meaningful_input_edit() {
 let old="table items:\n  label: text <=10\n  public 'fixture'\n  update <- allow\n  online only\n";
 let fill="backfill items derive(n: int ?):\n  {derived:n ?? 0}\n";
 let next=old.replace("  label:","  derived: int\n  label:")+fill;
 let later=next.replace("  label:","  n: int default 100\n  label:")+"mutation edit(n: int):\n  update items['a'] {n}\nmutation label():\n  update items['a'] {label:'changed'}\n";
 let mut e=engine(old);seed(&mut e,"items",json!({"id":"a","label":"old"}));adopt(&mut e,&next,2).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,&later,3).unwrap();write(&mut e,"label");
 adopt(&mut e,"query empty():\n  return true\n",4).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,&later,3).unwrap();assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","derived"),Value::Int(0));
 for n in [200,100] {let r=e.mutate("edit",None,Context::new("alice",std::collections::BTreeMap::from([("n".into(),Value::Int(n))]))).unwrap();assert!(matches!(r.state,WriteState::Sent{..}),"{r:?}");}
 adopt(&mut e,"query empty():\n  return true\n",4).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,&later,3).unwrap();assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","derived"),Value::Int(100));
}

 for reseed in [false,true] {

  let native=wire::row_from_json(&e.schema().tables["items"],&json!({"id":"native","n":3,"derived":9})).unwrap();
  e.dev_reset_at(if reseed {vec![("items".into(),native)]}else{vec![]},crate::now_ms()).unwrap();
  if !reseed {seed(&mut e,"items",json!({"id":"native","n":3,"derived":9}));}

#[test]
fn enum_replacement_accepts_original_preimages_and_preserves_native_outputs() {
 let old="table cues:\n  status: enum('standby','done')\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
 let second=old.replace("enum('standby','done')","enum('standby','complete','skipped')")+"backfill cues complete(status: enum('standby','done')):\n  {status:'complete' if status = 'done' else status}\n";
 let third=old.replace("enum('standby','done')","enum('standby','finished','skipped')")+"backfill cues finished(status: enum('standby','done','complete','skipped')):\n  {status:'finished' if status = 'done' or status = 'complete' else status}\n";
 let mut e=engine(old);seed(&mut e,"cues",json!({"id":"a","status":"done"}));adopt(&mut e,&second,2).unwrap();seed(&mut e,"cues",json!({"id":"native","status":"complete"}));
 adopt(&mut e,&third,3).unwrap();for id in ["a","native"]{assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"cues",id,"status"),Value::String("finished".into()));}
 adopt(&mut e,&second,2).unwrap();for id in ["a","native"]{assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"cues",id,"status"),Value::String("complete".into()));}
}

#[test]
fn source_expiry_observes_children_removed_in_the_same_release() {
 for action in ["cascade","set null","restrict"] {
  let optional=if action=="set null" {" ?"}else{""};
  let parent="table parents:\n  until: time\n  expire at .until\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
  let child=format!("table children:\n  parent: parents{optional} on delete {action}\n  cap 4 by parent\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n");
  let item="table items:\n  n: int\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
  let old=format!("{parent}{child}{item}");let next=format!("{parent}{}backfill items twice(n: int):\n  {{doubled:n * 2}}\n",item.replace("  n:","  doubled: int\n  n:"));
  let(s,p)=compile(&old);let mut e=Engine::new_release_prepared_at(Store::memory().unwrap(),s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(1,None),false,0).unwrap();
  let rows=[("parents",json!({"id":"p","until":50})),("children",json!({"id":"c","parent":"p"})),("items",json!({"id":"i","n":3}))];
  let rows=rows.into_iter().map(|(t,r)|(t.to_owned(),wire::row_from_json(&e.schema().tables[t],&r).unwrap())).collect::<Vec<_>>();e.seed_at(rows,0).unwrap();
  let(s,p)=compile(&next);let result=e.adopt_release_at(s,p,&ReleaseActivation::new(2,Some(1)),false,100);
  if action=="restrict" {let error=result.unwrap_err().to_string();assert!(error.contains("restrict"),"{error}");assert_eq!(e.store().count("parents").unwrap(),1);}else{
   result.unwrap();assert_eq!(e.store().count("parents").unwrap(),0);
   let tx=e.store_mut().transaction().unwrap();let t=tx.num("children").unwrap();
   let saved:Option<String>=tx.conn().query_row("SELECT data FROM _dormant_rows WHERE t=?1 AND id='c'",[t],|r|r.get(0)).optional().unwrap();
   if action=="cascade" {assert!(saved.is_none());}else{let saved:Value=serde_json::from_str(&saved.unwrap()).unwrap();assert_eq!(*saved.field("parent").unwrap(),Value::Null);}
  }
 }
}

#[test]
fn physically_sparse_defaults_are_interpreted_and_receipts_keep_that_interpretation() {
 for kind in ["int","int ?"] {
  let old="table items:\n  public 'fixture'\n  online only\n";
  let defaulted=old.replace("  public","  n: int default 3\n  public");
  let fill=format!("backfill items twice(n: {kind}):\n  {{doubled:(n ?? 0) * 2}}\n");
  let next=defaulted.replace("  n:","  doubled: int\n  n:")+&fill;
  let mut e=engine(old);seed(&mut e,"items",json!({"id":"a"}));adopt(&mut e,&defaulted,2).unwrap();
  assert!(row(&mut e,"items","a").field("n").is_err(),"fixture is physically sparse");
  adopt(&mut e,&next,3).unwrap();assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","doubled"),Value::Int(6));
  let later=next.replace("default 3","default 100");adopt(&mut e,&later,4).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,"query empty():\n  return true\n",5).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,&later,4).unwrap();
  assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","doubled"),Value::Int(6));
  let rollback=later.replace("  doubled: int\n","").replace(&fill,"");adopt(&mut e,&rollback,6).unwrap();adopt(&mut e,&later,4).unwrap();
  assert_eq!(field(&mut e,"items","a","doubled"),Value::Int(6),"rollback/forward keeps the original omitted-input interpretation");
 }
}

//! Human preview groups facts about one affected table/operation once.
// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#15-wave-15-preview-and-rollback-day5 — full evidence remains available in JSON and verbose output.
use std::collections::{BTreeMap, BTreeSet};
use snapback4_core::{Schema, ir::Program, store::DormantItem, successor::Step};
struct Group { warnings: Vec<String>, notes: Vec<String>, priority: u8 }
impl Default for Group { fn default() -> Self {Self {warnings:Vec::new(),notes:Vec::new(),priority:2}} }
fn table_prefix(text: &str, tables: &BTreeSet<String>) -> Option<String> {
    tables.iter().filter(|name|text.strip_prefix(name.as_str()).is_some_and(|tail|tail.is_empty() || tail.starts_with(['.',':',' ']))).max_by_key(|name|name.len()).cloned()
}
fn subject(text: &str, tables: &BTreeSet<String>, programs: &BTreeMap<String,Program>) -> String {
    // Read only generated subject positions, never arbitrary words inside an
    // authored predicate/refusal/value. Unknown formats remain release facts.
    if let Some(table)=table_prefix(text,tables) {return table;}
    for marker in ["table ","dependent ","backfill: "] {
        if let Some(tail)=text.strip_prefix(marker) && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
    }
    let prefix=text.split(';').next().unwrap_or(text);
    if text.starts_with("queries/counts ") && let Some((_,tail))=prefix.split_once(" read ") && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
    if text.starts_with("release ") && let Some((_,tail))=prefix.split_once(" safety dependencies on ") && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
    if text.starts_with("rollback users get release ") {
        if let Some((_,tail))=prefix.split_once(" quotas on ") && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
        if let Some((_,tail))=prefix.split_once("'s ") && let Some(table)=table_prefix(tail,tables) {return table;}
    }
    if text.starts_with("release ") {
        if let Some(token)=prefix.split_whitespace().last() && let Some((owner,effect))=token.rsplit_once('.') {
            if effect=="require" {return format!("operation {owner}");}
            if tables.contains(owner) && matches!(effect,"read"|"insert"|"update"|"delete") {return owner.into();}
        }
        for name in programs.keys() {
            if prefix.ends_with(&format!(" operation {name}")) {return format!("operation {name}");}
        }
    }
    "release behavior".into()
}
fn brief(text: &str) -> String {
    // Semicolons also separate authored guards and multiple cap declarations;
    // retaining the full fact avoids dropping their contracts or caveats.
    text.to_owned()
}
pub(super) fn print(current: Option<&Schema>, target: &Schema, programs: &BTreeMap<String,Program>, warnings: &[String], notes: &[String], steps: &[Step], items: &[DormantItem]) {
    let tables: BTreeSet<_>=target.tables.keys().chain(current.into_iter().flat_map(|s|s.tables.keys())).cloned().collect();
    let mut groups=BTreeMap::<String,Group>::new();
    for (warning, lines) in [(true,warnings),(false,notes)] {
        for line in lines {
            let group=groups.entry(subject(line,&tables,programs)).or_default();
            let priority=if line.contains("safety guard") || line.contains(".require;") {0} else if line.contains("confidentiality") || line.contains("safety rule") {1} else {2};
            group.priority=group.priority.min(priority);
            let text=if priority==0 {line.clone()} else {brief(line)};
            let dest=if warning {&mut group.warnings} else {&mut group.notes};
            if !dest.contains(&text) {dest.push(text);}
        }
    }
    for step in steps {
        let path=step.path.strip_prefix("tables.").unwrap_or(&step.path);
        let key=table_prefix(path,&tables).unwrap_or_else(||path.to_owned());
        if path.strip_prefix(&key).is_some_and(|tail|tail.starts_with(".indexes.")) {continue;}
        let group=groups.entry(key).or_default();
        // Keep each user-visible source change even when another fact already
        // names this table. Only index plumbing is verbose-only.
        let detail=brief(&format!("{}: {}",path.replace(".columns.","."),step.message));
        if !group.notes.contains(&detail) {group.notes.push(detail);}
    }
    let mut storage=BTreeMap::<String,[u64;3]>::new();
    for item in items.iter().filter(|item|item.rows>0 && item.kind!="backfill") {
        let name=table_prefix(&item.path,&tables).unwrap_or_else(||item.path.clone());
        let slot=match item.kind.as_str() {"column"=>1,"index"=>2,_=>0};
        storage.entry(name).or_default()[slot]+=item.rows;
    }
    for (name,[rows,cells,indexes]) in storage {
        groups.entry(name).or_default().notes.push(format!("retained: {rows} dormant rows, {cells} cells, {indexes} index entries"));
    }
    for item in items.iter().filter(|item|item.kind=="backfill" && item.rows>0) {
        let name=table_prefix(&item.path,&tables).unwrap_or_else(||item.path.clone());
        groups.entry(name).or_default().notes.push(format!("retained: {} private backfill preimages ({} bytes)",item.rows,item.bytes));
    }
    let mut groups=groups.into_iter().collect::<Vec<_>>();
    groups.sort_by_key(|(name,g)|(g.priority,name.clone()));
    for (name,mut group) in groups {
        let warning=!group.warnings.is_empty();
        group.warnings.append(&mut group.notes);
        println!("  {} {name}: {}{}",if warning {"WARNING"} else {"note:"},group.warnings.join("; "),if warning {"; verify these cases or preserve the current behavior in a bridge release"} else {""});
    }
}

    fn num(&self, name: &str) -> Result<i64, RuntimeError> {
        self.catalog.get(name).copied().ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Schema(format!("{name} is not installed in this store")))
    }

    pub fn get(&self, table: &str, id: &str) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
        let t = self.num(table)?;
        let data: Option<String> = self.tx.prepare_cached("SELECT data FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND id = ?2")?.query_row(params![t, id], |row| row.get(0)).optional()?;
        data.map(|data| serde_json::from_str(&data).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))).transpose()
    }

    /// The first row whose index components equal `key` exactly, with the
    /// number of entries examined (one, or zero).
    pub fn lookup(&self, table: &str, index_name: &str, index: &Index, key: &[Value]) -> Result<Option<Value>, RuntimeError> {
        if key.len() != index.components.len() {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Schema(format!("point read {table}.{index_name} supplied {} of {} key columns", key.len(), index.components.len())));
        }
        let prefix = key::encode(key);
        let rows = self.scan_keys(table, index_name, &prefix, &key::upper_bound(&prefix), Dir::Asc, 1)?;
        Ok(rows.into_iter().next().map(|(row, _)| row))
    }

    /// Rows under `prefix` in index order, bounded, at most `limit`. Each row
    /// comes with its stored key so a cursor can be minted from the last.
    pub fn scan(&self, table: &str, index_name: &str, prefix: &[Value], bounds: &Bounds, dir: Dir, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<(Value, Vec<u8>)>, RuntimeError> {
        let Some((lo, hi)) = crate::rows::scan_range(prefix, bounds, dir) else { return Ok(Vec::new());
        };
        self.scan_keys(table, index_name, &lo, &hi, dir, limit)
    }

    fn scan_keys(&self, table: &str, index_name: &str, lo: &[u8], hi: &[u8], dir: Dir, limit: usize) -> Result<Vec<(Value, Vec<u8>)>, RuntimeError> {
        let t = self.num(table)?;
        let ti = self.num(&format!("{table}.{index_name}"))?;
        let mut statement = self.tx.prepare_cached(scan_sql(dir))?;
        let mut rows = statement.query(params![t, ti, lo, hi, limit as i64])?;
        let mut out = Vec::new();
        while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
            let data = row.get_ref(0)?.as_str().map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
            out.push((serde_json::from_str(data).map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?, row.get(1)?,
            ));
        }
        Ok(out)
    }

    /// How many entries sit under `prefix`, counting at most `limit`.
    pub fn count_prefix(&self, table: &str, index_name: &str, prefix: &[Value], limit: u64) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        let ti = self.num(&format!("{table}.{index_name}"))?;
        let base = key::encode(prefix);
        let hi = key::upper_bound(&base);
        let count: i64 = self.tx.prepare_cached("SELECT COUNT(*) FROM (SELECT 1 FROM i WHERE ti = ?1 AND k >= ?2 AND k < ?3 LIMIT ?4)")?.query_row(params![ti, base, hi, limit as i64], |row| row.get(0))?;
        Ok(count as u64)
    }

    /// Write a row image: a fresh insert when `old` is none, else a replace
    /// that touches only the index entries whose keys changed (a `words`
    /// index has one per token). Returns the number of entries written.
    pub fn put(&self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, row: &Value, old: Option<&Value>) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.put_indexed(table_name, table, row, old, "INSERT INTO i(ti, k, id) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)")
    }

    /// A replacement loader has already cleared the rows and created its

    pub fn put_loading_indexes(&self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, row: &Value) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.put_indexed(table_name, table, row, None, "INSERT INTO temp._device_index_load(ti, k, id) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)")
    }

    fn put_indexed(&self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, row: &Value, old: Option<&Value>, insert_index: &str) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.clear_activation_scan();
        if table.ephemeral.is_some() { return Err(RuntimeError::Store("durable transaction cannot write an ephemeral table".into())); }
        let t = self.num(table_name)?;
        let id = row.field("id")?.as_str()?;
        narrowed::check_write(self,table_name,table,row,old)?;
        backfills::observe_write(self,t,id,table,row,old)?;
        let keys = crate::rows::index_write(table_name, table, row, old, id)?;
        self.changes.borrow_mut().record(table_name, table, old, Some(row));
        let data = canonical_json(row);
        let sql = if old.is_some() { "UPDATE r SET data = ?3 WHERE t = ?1 AND id = ?2" } else { "INSERT INTO r(t, id, data) VALUES (?1, ?2, ?3)" };
        self.tx.prepare_cached(sql)?.execute(params![t, id, data])?;
        let mut insert = self.tx.prepare_cached(insert_index)?;
        let mut entries = 0;
        for crate::rows::IndexWrite { name, before, after } in keys {
            if before == after { continue; }
            let ti = self.num(&format!("{table_name}.{name}"))?;
            for key in before.iter().filter(|key| !after.contains(key)) {
                self.conn().prepare_cached("DELETE FROM i WHERE ti = ?1 AND k = ?2")?.execute(params![ti, key])?;
                entries += 1;
            }
            for key in after.iter().filter(|key| !before.contains(key)) {
                insert.execute(params![ti, key, id])?;
                entries += 1;
            }
        }
        entries += self.update_cap_counts(table_name, table, old, Some(row))?;
        Ok(entries)
    }

    pub fn delete(&self, table_name: &str, table: &Table, old: &Value) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        self.clear_activation_scan();
        if table.ephemeral.is_some() { return Err(RuntimeError::Store("durable transaction cannot write an ephemeral table".into())); }
        let t = self.num(table_name)?;
        self.changes.borrow_mut().record(table_name, table, Some(old), None);
        let id = old.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
        dormant::delete(self,t,&id,table_name)?;
        self.conn().prepare_cached("DELETE FROM r WHERE t = ?1 AND id = ?2")?.execute(params![t, id])?;
        let mut entries = 0;
        for (index_name, index) in &table.indexes {
            let ti = self.num(&format!("{table_name}.{index_name}"))?;
            for key in stored_index_keys(table, index, old, &id) {
                self.conn().prepare_cached("DELETE FROM i WHERE ti = ?1 AND k = ?2")?.execute(params![ti, key])?;
                entries += 1;
            }
        }
        entries += self.update_cap_counts(table_name, table, Some(old), None)?;
        Ok(entries)
    }

    pub fn next_seq(&self) -> Result<u64, RuntimeError> {
        Ok(self.tx.prepare_cached("SELECT COALESCE(MAX(seq), 0) + 1 FROM _commits")?.query_row([], |row| row.get::<_, i64>(0))? as u64)
    }

    }

        )?;

//! Writes: the four words, their rules, the constraints (unique, cap,
//! immutable, append-only, after-insert), maintained aggregates, and the
//! partition events every row change produces.

use super::runner::Runner;
use super::validate::validate_row;
use crate::error::{MeterKind, RuntimeError};
use crate::partition;
use crate::rows::index_values;
use crate::rows::{Bounds, Dir};
use crate::schema::{Constraint, Effect, Table, materialize_optional_fields};
use crate::value::{Supplied, Value, canonical_json};

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
pub(crate) enum Origin {
    Source,
    Maintained,
    LiveAuthority,
}

#[derive(Clone)]
pub(super) struct FinalExistsWitness {
    table: String,
    row: Value,
    constraint: usize,
}

#[path = "write_references.rs"]
mod references;
#[path = "write_target.rs"]
pub(crate) mod target;

impl Runner<'_> {
    pub(super) fn insert(&mut self, table: &str, row: Supplied) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
        self.insert_mode(table, row, false).map(|_| ())
    }

    pub(super) fn insert_if_absent(&mut self, table: &str, row: Supplied) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        self.insert_mode(table, row, true)
    }

    fn insert_mode(&mut self, table_name: &str, row: Supplied, if_absent: bool) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        if self.device && self.schema.tables[table_name].not_before.is_some() {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(
                "a mutation touching a `not before` table runs on the server".into(),
            ));
        }
        if self.device && if_absent && self.schema.tables[table_name].through.is_some() {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction("insert if absent on a read-through child queues without a row".into()));
        }
        self.target_attempt(table_name, |runner| {
            let mark = runner.meter.mark();
            let result = runner.insert_attempt(table_name, row, if_absent, None).map_err(|error| error.authorization_context(table_name, Effect::Insert));
            // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — denied direct allocations hide deferred
            // read witnesses and counter work just as NOT_FOUND hides targets.
            if matches!(&result, Err(RuntimeError::Rule { effect: Effect::Insert, .. } | RuntimeError::AuthorizationBudget { .. }))
                && runner.schema.tables.get(table_name).is_some_and(|table| !table.sequences.is_empty()) {
                runner.meter.restore(mark);
            }
            result
        })
    }

    fn insert_attempt(&mut self, table_name: &str, row: Supplied, if_absent: bool, upsert_index: Option<&str>) -> Result<bool, RuntimeError> {
        self.refuse_engine_owned(table_name, Effect::Insert)?;
        self.refuse_receipt_fields(table_name, &row, true)?;
        self.refuse_recorded(table_name, &row)?;
        let supplied_sequence = super::sequences::refuse_fields(&self.schema.tables[table_name], table_name, &row);
        // A directly supplied field is a payload error before any lookup;
        // only an upsert's copied address waits for insert authority.
        if upsert_index.is_none() && supplied_sequence.is_err() { return supplied_sequence.map(|_| false); }
        let supplied = row.clone();
        let row = self.with_defaults(table_name, row)?;
        if self.schema.tables[table_name].ephemeral.is_some() { self.meter.heap(row.heap_bytes())?; }
        let row = row.ephemeral(&self.schema.tables[table_name], self.context.now.unwrap_or(0))?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.014#4-the-capture — reserve, then stamp the parent capture before any rule sees the image.
        self.reserve_capture(&self.schema.tables[table_name])?;
        let row = self.capture_insert(table_name, row)?;
        let table = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
        let independent = !table.sequences.is_empty() && !super::rules::deciding_fields(table_name, table, &table.rules.insert)
            .iter().any(|field| table.sequences.contains_key(field));
        // An independent denial must never consult a hidden read witness.
        let authorized = independent && self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Insert, None, &row)?;
        if independent && !authorized {
            return Err(if upsert_index.is_some() { self.no_write_target() } else { self.rule_refusal(table_name, Effect::Insert, "insert rule") });
        }
        if !table.sequences.is_empty() {
            // Admission reserves the worst case before either read verdict;
            // restoring a refusal alone cannot hide a boundary abort.
            // An independent insert rule was already prepaid and evaluated.
            // Only still-pending checks belong in this preflight allowance.
            let insert_checks = if authorized { 0 } else { 1 + u64::from(upsert_index.is_some() && supplied_sequence.is_ok()) };
            self.reserve_sequence_authorization(table, &row, insert_checks)?;
        }
        // @ref LLP 3000.015#2 — an unreadable allocation cannot expose counter,
        // uniqueness or cap state, even to a principal allowed to insert.
        if !self.sequence_insert_readable(table_name, &row)? {
            self.refusing_clause(table_name, "sequence read authority");
            return Err(if upsert_index.is_some() { self.no_write_target() } else { self.rule_refusal(table_name, Effect::Insert, "sequence read authority") });
        }
        if let Err(error) = supplied_sequence {
            // @ref LLP 3000.007#17 — absent upserts decide insert authority before field diagnostics.
            // A target key may supply an ordinal even when the patch does not.
            if !authorized && !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Insert, None, &row)? {
                return Err(if upsert_index.is_some() { self.no_write_target() } else { self.rule_refusal(table_name, Effect::Insert, "insert rule") });
            }
            return Err(if upsert_index.is_some() { self.no_write_target() } else { error });
        }
        if upsert_index.is_some() {
            self.authorize_fields(table_name, &row, &supplied).map_err(|_| self.no_write_target())?;
        } else { self.authorize_fields(table_name, &row, &supplied)?; }
        // The image copy an event slot costs is the writer's own supplied bytes (LLP 3000.015 §1).
        let image_bytes = row.heap_bytes();
        let (row, sequence_full) = self.sequence_fields(table_name, row)?;
        let row = self.receipt_insert_fields(table_name, row)?;
        if let Some(index) = upsert_index {
            if self.device { self.prove_upsert_insert(table_name, index, &row)?; }
            // Preserve upsert's target preflight before the ordinary insert checks;
            // only this first authority refusal is an undisclosed target miss.
            if !authorized && !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Insert, None, &row)? { return Err(self.no_write_target()); }
            if sequence_full { return Err(super::sequences::exhausted()); }
            // Engine event slots are stamped after predecessor/sequence checks,
            // just as on an ordinary insert; preflight validates authored fields.
            if let Err(error) = super::validate::validate_before_slots(self.schema, table_name, &row) {
                return Err(if matches!(error, RuntimeError::Input(_)) && !self.context.is_system() { self.no_write_target() } else { error });
            }
        }
        if !authorized && !self.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Insert, None, &row)? {
            return Err(self.rule_refusal(table_name, Effect::Insert, "insert rule"));
        }
        // Retry keys independent of engine allocation still identify a no-op
        // at the ceiling. Never use the clamped authority candidate as a key.
        if sequence_full && if_absent {
            let table = &self.schema.tables[table_name];
            for (name, index) in table.indexes.iter().filter(|(_, index)| {
                index.unique && index.columns().iter().all(|column| !table.sequences.contains_key(column))
            }) {
                let key = index_values(index, &row);
                if key.contains(&Value::Null) { continue; }
                if self.collision_lookup(table_name, name, index, &key, None, Effect::Insert)?.is_some() {
                    self.observe_sequence_columns(table_name, &row, &index.columns(), true)?;
                    return Ok(false);
                }
            }
        }
        if sequence_full { return Err(super::sequences::exhausted()); }
        let row = self.record_insert(table_name, row)?;
        let row = self.with_asset_facts(table_name, row, None, None)?;
        if if_absent {
            for (name, index) in table.indexes.iter().filter(|(_, index)| index.unique) {
                let key = index_values(index, &row);
                if key.iter().any(|value| *value == Value::Null) {
                    continue;
                }
                if self.collision_lookup(table_name, name, index, &key, None, Effect::Insert)?.is_some() {
                    self.observe_sequence_columns(table_name, &row, &index.columns(), true)?;
                    return Ok(false);
                }
            }
        }
        let id = row.field("id")?.as_str()?.to_owned();
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — if-absent's insert arm needs the same image, unique-population and cap proof as upsert.
        // Upsert mints its insert id; if-absent may instead supply one.
        // Only a freshly minted id can skip the primary-key absence proof.
        let minted = self.context.minted_ids.contains(&id);
        let proof = if !self.device { None } else if minted {
            table.indexes.iter().find(|(name, index)| {
                    name.as_str() != "byId" && index.unique && !index_values(index, &row).contains(&Value::Null)
                })
                .map(|(name, _)| name.as_str()).or_else(|| {
                    table.constraints.iter().any(|c| matches!(c, Constraint::Cap { .. })).then_some("byId")
                })
        } else { Some("byId") };
        if if_absent && let Some(index) = proof.or(self.device.then_some("byId")) {
            self.prove_upsert_insert(table_name, index, &row)?;
        }
        // An upsert has already resolved this exact address (or minted the id)
        // and reserved both target proofs. Retiring an expired predecessor
        // uses that same allowance, not a third read-rule reservation.
        let collision_probes = if upsert_index.is_some() { 0 } else { super::rules::rule_probes(&table.rules.read) };
        let has_through_children = self.schema.children(table_name).next().is_some();
        let has_children = has_through_children || self.schema.is_referenced(table_name);
        let predecessor = self.authorized_scan(&[(MeterKind::RuleProbes, collision_probes)], |runner, allowance| {
            let existing = runner.tx.get(allowance, table_name, &id)?;
            if let Some(row) = &existing {
                if !runner.expired(table, row) { runner.visible_collision(table_name, row, Effect::Insert, "unique id")?; }
                // An expired predecessor's read rule cannot veto actionable
                // reference retirement. A declared read-through child is
                // different: a non-reader cannot probe whether hidden
                // physical children retain the predecessor.
                else if has_through_children && !runner.check_rule(table_name, Effect::Read, None, row)? {
                    return Err(runner.rule_refusal(table_name, Effect::Insert, "unique id"));
                }
            }
            Ok(existing)
        })?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.039#6.4 — a logical device miss cannot prove there is
        // no hidden, expired physical predecessor whose retirement would run
        // reference actions. Controller-minted identities are the existing
        // fresh-address proof; every other referenced same-id insert queues.
        if self.device && predecessor.is_none() && has_children && table.is_expiring() && !minted {
            return Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(format!(
                "same-id insert into referenced {table_name} needs the server's physical predecessor check; queued without predicted rows"
            )));
        }
        if predecessor.as_ref().is_none_or(|old| self.expired(table, old)) && has_children {
            let mark = self.meter.mark();
            if self.physical_children(table_name, &Value::Id(id.clone()))? {
                // The bounded probes have completed. Their occupancy is not
                // disclosed by the collision's logical meter or heap peak.
                self.meter.restore(mark);
                return Err(if predecessor.is_some() {
                    RuntimeError::Constraint(format!("{table_name} already has a row with id {id}"))
                } else { self.rule_refusal(table_name, Effect::Insert, "parent identity has stored children") });
            }
        }
        if let Some(existing) = &predecessor {
            if !self.expired(table, &existing) {
                return Err(RuntimeError::Constraint(format!("{table_name} already has a row with id {id}")));
            }
            // The expired predecessor is internal authorization work, not a
            // disclosed examination (LLP 3000.015 §§1–2).
            self.retire_expired_row(table_name, existing)?;
        }
        // Retiring an expired predecessor can cascade a source row whose
        // contribution determines this image's maintained columns. Initialize
        // them from the post-retirement private totals. Maintained columns are
        // forbidden from constraints and authority, so the earlier collision
        // and authorization preflights need only the authored image.
        let row = self.birth_columns(table_name, row)?;
        super::validate::validate_before_slots(self.schema, table_name, &row)?;
        // @ref LLP 3000.007#20.5 — an authored plain insert predicts unproved; a later refusal is then the server's
        // to report. The engine's own timeline writes are not the author's prediction.
        if let Some(index) = proof.filter(|_| {
            !if_absent && upsert_index.is_none() && !self.unproved_write && self.timeline_authority.is_none()
        }) {
            // An earlier unknown fact already makes this prediction unproved.
            // Otherwise the proof's own unknown fact is not the prediction's.
            self.unproved_write = self.missing_fact.is_some();
            if !self.unproved_write {
                let beyond = self.beyond_horizon;
                let proved = self.device_work(|runner| runner.prove_upsert_insert(table_name, index, &row));
                (self.beyond_horizon, self.missing_fact) = (beyond, None);
                match proved { Err(RuntimeError::Prediction(_)) => self.unproved_write = true, other => other? }
            }
        }
        // Retirement released every logical key and cap slot. Treat the new
        // image as a fresh insert: an unchanged secondary key can now belong
        // to another live row and must be probed again.
        self.check_constraints(table_name, None, &row, Effect::Insert)?;

                    generation, schema_hash, indexes: indexes.clone(),

            }
        }
        let after = identity(tx.conn())?;
        super::live_activation::finalize(&tx)?;
        let result = finish(&tx)?;
        super::live_activation::cleanup(&tx)?;
        report.phase("metadata", &mut phase);
        tx.commit()?;
        report.phase("commit", &mut phase);
        // Reopening an unchanged backend must not announce a new adoption.
        self.adoption_report = if changed || reset { report } else { Default::default() };
        // Historical ordinals stay in _catalog, but no runtime transaction can address memory tables.
        catalog.retain(|name,_| {
            !schema.tables.iter().any(|(table,t)| {
                t.ephemeral.is_some() && (name == table || name.starts_with(&format!("{table}.")))
            })
        });
        self.catalog = catalog;
        self.identity = after;
        self.accept_open();
        Ok((generation, result))
    }
}

// @ref LLP 3000.019#3.6 — a key-bound proof must be invalidated even by direct SQL edits.
fn index_key_guards(conn: &Connection) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    let limit = crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES;
    let insert = format!("_index_keys_insert_{limit}");
    let update = format!("_index_keys_update_{limit}");
    let installed: i64 = conn.query_row(
        "SELECT count(*) FROM sqlite_schema WHERE type = 'trigger' AND name IN (?1, ?2)",
        params![insert, update], |r| r.get(0),
    )?;
    if installed != 2 {
        // A predecessor without both guards could have retained a proof across
        // physical edits. Install and revalidate in this activation transaction.
        conn.execute("DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key = 'index_keys_validated'", [])?;
        conn.execute_batch(&format!(
            "CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS {insert} AFTER INSERT ON i WHEN length(NEW.k) > {limit}
             BEGIN DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key = 'index_keys_validated'; END;
             CREATE TRIGGER IF NOT EXISTS {update} AFTER UPDATE OF k ON i WHEN length(NEW.k) > {limit}
             BEGIN DELETE FROM _meta WHERE key = 'index_keys_validated'; END;"
        ))?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

/// Equal prefixes are adjacent in an index. Validate uniqueness and caps
/// in one bounded pass per invariant, retaining one key rather than one
/// allocation for every group/row in a potentially large activation.
fn validate_groups(tx: &Tx<'_>, table: &str, index: &str, prefix_len: usize, max: u64, nulls_distinct: bool) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    use crate::{error::MeterKind, meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter}, rows::word_heap as heap};
    // Only encoded group keys matter. Fetching source images here would
    // recreate an unmetered 500-row payload buffer after the metered rebuild.
    let mut statement = tx.conn().prepare_cached("SELECT k FROM i WHERE ti = ?1 ORDER BY k")?;
    let mut rows = statement.query([tx.num(&format!("{table}.{index}"))?])?;
    let mut previous: Option<Vec<Value>> = None;
    let mut count = 0;
    let mut visited = 0;
    let mut meter = Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort);
    while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
        if visited % 256 == 0 {
            meter = Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort);
            meter.at(&format!("adopt {table}.{index} groups"));
            meter.once(crate::meter::HeapSite::SqliteColumns, 2 * tx.page_size)?;
        }
        visited += 1;
        let scratch = meter.mark();
        meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
        let key = row.get_ref(0)?.as_blob().map_err(|e| RuntimeError::Store(e.to_string()))?;
        meter.heap(heap::key_decode(key.len(), key.len()))?;
        if let Some(values) = &previous {
            meter.heap(heap::slots::<Value>(values.len()))?;
            crate::engine::authorized_scan::InternalLedger::with_meter(&mut meter, |meter, scope| {
                for value in values { value.retained_internal(scope).charge(meter, scope)?; }
                Ok::<_, RuntimeError>(())
            })?;
        }
        let mut group = crate::key::decode(key).ok_or_else(|| RuntimeError::Store("invalid rebuilt index key".into()))?;
        group.truncate(prefix_len);
        if !(nulls_distinct && group.contains(&Value::Null)) {
            if previous.as_ref() == Some(&group) { count += 1; } else { previous = Some(group); count = 1; }
            if count > max { return Err(RuntimeError::Constraint(format!("cannot activate {table}.{index}: existing group exceeds {}", if nulls_distinct { "a unique key".to_owned() } else { format!("cap {max}") }))); }
        }
        meter.release_heap(scratch);
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn contains_asset_type(kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType) -> bool {
    use crate::schema::ColumnType::*;
    match kind { Optional(inner) | List { of: inner, .. } | ListRange { of: inner, .. } => {
            contains_asset_type(inner)
        }
        Image { .. } | Video { .. } | File { .. } => true, _ => false }
}
pub(super) fn validate_assets(tx: &Tx<'_>, kind: &crate::schema::ColumnType, value: Option<&Value>) -> Result<(), RuntimeError> {
    use crate::assets::AssetKind;
    use crate::schema::ColumnType::*;
    match (kind, value) {
        (Optional(inner), Some(value)) => validate_assets(tx, inner, Some(value)),
        (List { of, .. } | ListRange { of, .. }, Some(Value::Array(values))) => { for value in values { validate_assets(tx, of, Some(value))?; } Ok(()) }
        (Image { .. } | Video { .. } | File { .. }, Some(value)) => {
            let (wanted, max, types) = kind.asset_leaf().expect("an asset leaf");
            if let Some(id) = crate::assets::asset_id(Some(value)) {
                if let Some(asset) = tx.asset(id)? {
                    if asset.kind != wanted { return Err(RuntimeError::Asset { code: "E_ASSET_TYPE", message: format!("cannot activate: {id} is {}, not {}", asset.kind.word(), wanted.word()) }); }
                    if wanted == AssetKind::File && !crate::assets::file_accepts(types, &asset.content_type) { return Err(RuntimeError::Asset { code: "E_ASSET_TYPE", message: format!("cannot activate: {id} is {}, which the column no longer accepts", asset.content_type) }); }
                    if asset.bytes > u64::from(max) { return Err(RuntimeError::Asset { code: "E_ASSET_TOO_LARGE", message: format!("cannot activate: {id} has {} bytes; the column takes at most {max}", asset.bytes) }); }
                }
            }
            Ok(())
        }
        _ => Ok(())
    }
}

snapback4/JOURNAL.md:2271:The later Grok correction review exposed a device that had acquired a row before membership expiry, missed its deletion during the unauthorized gap, then rejoined. snapback4/JOURNAL.md:2277:## 2026-09-13 — rotated credentials preserve live observations
snapback4/JOURNAL.md:2279:The received Grok integration review independently found the stale-token write race and its online-only read variant. A delayed old-bearer query could install an authentication refusal after refresh succeeded, with no later table change to rerun the watch. The regression first reproduced that stuck observation. //! A process-local clock for development and explicitly classified staging stores.
use snapback4_core::error::Refusal;
use std::time::{Duration, Instant};

const MAX_TIME: i64 = snapback4_core::value::I53_MAX;

pub fn input(message: impl Into<String>) -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_INPUT", "clock", message).guide("clock") }
pub fn release() -> Refusal { Refusal::new("E_CLOCK_DEV_ONLY", "clock", "clock controls require dev or a deploy --staging store; production always uses wall time").guide("clock") }

/// Isolated time tests stay inside an assigned range, or request a free port.
pub(crate) fn isolated_command() -> String {
    isolated_range(std::env::var("PORT_LO").ok().as_deref(), std::env::var("PORT_HI").ok().as_deref())
}
fn isolated_range(lo: Option<&str>, hi: Option<&str>) -> String {
    match (lo.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok()), hi.and_then(|n| n.parse::<u16>().ok())) {
        (Some(lo), Some(hi)) if lo > 0 && hi >= lo => format!("dev --memory --port {lo}-{hi} within the current range"),
        _ => "dev --memory --port 0".into(),
    }
}

pub fn duration(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if text.starts_with('-') { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
    let text = text.strip_prefix('+').unwrap_or(text);
    let split = text.bytes().position(|b| !b.is_ascii_digit()).unwrap_or(text.len());
    let (number, unit) = text.split_at(split);
    let multiplier = match unit { "ms" => 1, "s" => 1_000, "m" => 60_000, "h" => 3_600_000, "d" => 86_400_000, "w" => 604_800_000, _ => 0 };
    number.parse::<i64>().ok().and_then(|n| n.checked_mul(multiplier)).filter(|n| *n > 0 && *n <= MAX_TIME)
        .ok_or_else(|| input("expected a positive whole duration with ms, s, m, h, d or w, such as +25h"))
}

pub fn offset(text: &str) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    if let Some(rest) = text.strip_prefix('-') { duration(rest).map(|n| -n) } else { duration(text) }
}

fn time(value: Option<i64>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    value.filter(|n| (0..=MAX_TIME).contains(n)).ok_or_else(|| input("time must be Unix milliseconds in 0..9007199254740991; choose a smaller time or duration"))
}

pub fn run_now(text: Option<&String>) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
    let now = snapback4_core::now_ms();
    match text {
        None => Ok(now),
        Some(text) if text.starts_with('+') => time(now.checked_add(duration(text)?)),
        Some(text) => time(text.parse().ok()),
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Debug)]
pub struct Clock {
    dev: bool,
    base: i64,
    offset: i64,
    started: Instant,
    epoch: String,
    revision: u64,
    #[cfg(test)]
    frozen: bool,
}

impl Clock {
    pub fn new(dev: bool, offset: i64) -> Result<Self, Refusal> {
        if !dev && offset != 0 { return Err(release()); }
        Ok(Self { dev, offset, base: time(snapback4_core::now_ms().checked_add(offset))?, started: Instant::now(),
            epoch: snapback4_core::ids::mint(snapback4_core::now_ms(), &mut snapback4_core::ids::Mint::default()).map_err(|e| e.refusal())?, revision: 0, #[cfg(test)] frozen: false })
    }
    #[cfg(test)]
    pub(crate) fn freeze(&mut self, now: i64) { self.base = now; self.frozen = true; }
    pub fn now(&self) -> i64 {
        #[cfg(test)] if self.frozen { return self.base; }
        if !self.dev { return snapback4_core::now_ms(); }
        self.base.saturating_add(self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64).min(MAX_TIME)
    }
    /// Identifies samples taken before/after a restart or deliberate clock jump.
    pub fn offset(&self) -> i64 { self.offset }
    pub fn revision(&self) -> String { format!("{}:{}", self.epoch, self.revision) }
    pub fn presence_now(&self) -> i64 {
        // Production grace is elapsed real time, unaffected by wall-clock corrections.
        if self.dev { self.now() } else { self.started.elapsed().as_millis().min(MAX_TIME as u128) as i64 }
    }
    /// Back to wall time: the offset `--clock-offset` and every advance added
    /// is dropped (a development reset's `{"clock":"reset"}`).
    pub fn reset(&mut self) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = 0;
        self.base = snapback4_core::now_ms();
        self.started = Instant::now();
        #[cfg(test)] { self.frozen = false; }
        Ok(self.base)
    }
    pub fn advance(&mut self, milliseconds: i64) -> Result<i64, Refusal> {
        if !self.dev { return Err(release()); }
        if milliseconds <= 0 { return Err(input("clock advance cannot move backwards; use a positive duration such as +2m")); }
        let next = time(self.now().checked_add(milliseconds))?;
        let offset = self.offset.checked_add(milliseconds).ok_or_else(|| input("cumulative clock offset overflow"))?;
        self.revision += 1;
        self.offset = offset;
        self.base = next;
        self.started = Instant::now();
        Ok(next)
    }
}

/// The control CLI only talks to a loopback dev host. It does not open its store.
pub fn command(options: &crate::verbs::Options) -> i32 {
    let result = (|| -> Result<String, String> {
        if options.positionals.len() != 2 || options.positionals[0] != "advance" {
            return Err(input(format!("usage: {}", crate::cli_flags::synopsis("clock"))).to_string());
        }
        duration(&options.positionals[1]).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        let release_path = options.flags.get("release").map(|dir| std::path::PathBuf::from(dir).join("store.sqlite"));
        if release_path.is_some() && options.flags.contains_key("port") { return Err("clock --release does not accept --port".into()); }
        let (address, instance, token) = if let Some(path) = &release_path {
            let store = snapback4_core::Store::open_read_only(path).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
            if store.meta("deployment_environment").map_err(|e|e.to_string())?.as_deref() != Some("staging") { return Err(release().to_string()); }
            let address = crate::store_owner::inspector_address(path).ok_or("staging clock requires a running serve")?;
            let session = crate::serve::token::mint_live(path, "clock", 1).map_err(|(_,error)|error)?;
            (address,None,Some(session.token))
        } else { let (address,instance)=crate::verbs::dev_address(options)?; (address,instance,None) };
        let body = serde_json::json!({"duration":options.positionals[1],"eachBoundary":options.flags.contains_key("each-boundary")}).to_string();
        // The common HTTP/1.0 exchange is EOF-delimited and bounds replies at
        // 64 MiB, enough for the preflight's complete explicit window report.
        let response = if let Some(token) = &token {
            crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_authorized(address,"POST","/dev/clock/advance",None,Some(token),&body,Duration::from_secs(60))
        } else { crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange_dev(address, "/dev/clock/advance", instance.as_deref(), &body, Duration::from_secs(60)) };
        let (status, json) = response.map_err(|error| {
            let evidence = crate::verbs::run_forward::exchange(address, "GET", "/dev/status", None, "", Duration::from_secs(5)).ok()
                .map(|(_, status)| format!("now={}, skewMs={}", status["now"], status["skewMs"]))
                .unwrap_or_else(|| "clock status unavailable".into());
            format!("clock advance reply failed at {address}: {error}; time may already have advanced ({evidence}); inspect /dev/status and queued work before retrying; for an isolated dev pass --port N")
        })?;
        if let Some(denied) = json.get("denied") {
            let clock = json["message"].as_str().map(|message| format!("; time remains advanced: {message}")).unwrap_or_default();
            return Err(format!("{}: {}{clock}\n  guide: clock", denied["code"].as_str().unwrap_or("E_CLOCK_INPUT"), denied["message"].as_str().unwrap_or("clock advance failed")));
        }
        if status != 200 { return Err(format!("dev refused clock advance: {json}")); }
        Ok(json.to_string())
    })();
    match result { Ok(body) => { println!("{body}"); 0 }, Err(error) => { eprintln!("{error}"); 1 } }
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod isolated_tests {
    #[test]
    fn time_test_guidance_uses_only_valid_assigned_ranges_or_a_free_port() {
        assert_eq!(super::isolated_range(Some("24000"), Some("24009")), "dev --memory --port 24000-24009 within the current range");
        for (lo,hi) in [(None,None),(Some("0"),Some("3")),(Some("4"),Some("3")),(Some("bad"),Some("3"))] {
            assert_eq!(super::isolated_range(lo,hi), "dev --memory --port 0");
        }
    }
}

## Summary

Snapback 4 is one of two parallel candidates for the successor to Snapback 2,
and the sibling of Snapback 3, not its successor. It builds
[LLP 2000.000](./2000.000-keep-the-core-flip-two-substrates.rfc.md) as
written: the Snapback 2 core kept verbatim, two substrates flipped up front —
resources metered at runtime instead of priced statically, and a client that
replicates the viewer's declared partition instead of caching receipted
results — proved first on the hub fixture, with a deterministic simulator as
the primary harness. Snapback 3 ([LLP 2000](./2000-snapback3.rfc.md), led by
Codex / GPT-6 Astra) keeps the same two questions open and discovers their
answers in its first slice. Snapback 2 ([LLP 1000](./1000-snapback2.explainer.md))
continues as the incumbent and the control. All three are judged by one
pre-registered comparison on one clock.

This document records the author's decisions of 2026-09-12 that created the
track, restates the bet on one page so a reader can orient without the brief,
fixes the bakeoff protocol, draws the fence, and plans the first four weeks.
The design argument and its evidence stay in LLP 2000.000. Only running code
will bind (`rules/RULES.md`).

## 1. Decisions (author, 2026-09-12)

On 2026-09-12 Charlie Cheever asked whether Claude Fable 5.1 should lead a
Snapback 4 while Codex / GPT-6 Astra leads Snapback 3 and Snapback 2
continues, "and see which one turns out best." The lead answered yes with
conditions; the author accepted them ("Sounds good") and asked for this
document. The decisions below are therefore the lead's proposal as accepted
by the author. Where the author has not separately ruled, the text says so.

1. **Three tracks, one comparison.** Snapback 2 continues as the incumbent
   and the control. Snapback 3 builds LLP 2000; Snapback 4 builds LLP
   2000.000. This is a bakeoff of *bets* — discover the substrates in the
   slice versus decide them first — not of models. The result will say more
   about the bets than about the leads, and §3 is written so that it can.
2. **The name is Snapback 4.** Siblings, not a sequence: "4" does not mean
   "after 3." A separate number gives the track its own corpus root,
   directory, package identity and data directory with no rename when the
   bakeoff resolves, and files never move in LLP. If Snapback 4 loses, it is
   a number that never shipped. "Snapback 3b" was considered and rejected:
   it reads as a variant of 3, and this is a different bet.
3. **Snapback 4 builds LLP 2000.000 as written.** Its §14 open questions are
   the lead's to decide inside the track, recorded in §7 as they are
   decided. The author rules on the bar, the comparison and promotion (§3).
4. **One owner on the core.** The lead writes the engine, the store and the
   client contract. Codex lanes build the fixture generator, the reference
   applications, the device witnesses and the periphery. Blind reviews from
   two model families are reserved for the two disclosure-sensitive
   mechanisms: partition inversion of read rules (LLP 2000.000 §7.1) and
   the meter's cut behaviour on non-uniform scans (LLP 2000.000 §6). This
   departs from the standing rule that Codex codes and Claude orchestrates,
   deliberately, for the core only.
5. **The clock is four weeks** from the first commit under `snapback4/` to
   the first slice running on the hub fixture. At the clock the author kills
   the track, merges its substrates into a survivor, or continues it. There
   is no third month without a ruling.
6. **Shared and not shared.** Shared with Snapback 3: the LLP corpus, the
   Clique harness and scorers, the fixtures, the briefs, and the simulator
   once either track has one. Not shared: code, except the Snapback 2 pieces
   both are expected to copy (LLP 2000.000 §5.1).
7. **Snapback 2 keeps shipping and freezes new substrate work for the
   duration.** Fix-forward, the loop bar, acquisition and papercuts continue;
   no new certificate axes, client custody mechanisms or ceiling changes.
   This is accepted here as a condition of the bakeoff. Making it binding on
   concurrent Snapback 2 sessions needs one line in `rules/NOT-DOING.md`'s
   Moves ledger, which this document does not write.
8. **Reading load.** This root, updated in place, and one append-only
   journal, `snapback4/JOURNAL.md`. Sub-LLPs only for a decision that must
   outlive the journal. No panels beyond decision 4's two reviews.

## 2. The bet on one page

**Keep verbatim from Snapback 2** (LLP 2000.000 §5.1): the rule language
with its uniformity and hoist analysis, `decided_true` and the
structural-fact refusals; one data language, Quarry, with `--` comments,
`require … else CODE`, `shape`, `merge`, `walk`, `chunk`; the value model
and its conformance corpus; typed read and write states with no silent state
and the refusal envelope `{code, family, site, message, rewrite, guide}`; the
successor classifier (widening additive, checked narrowing, exact projection
ownership); `deliver`'s engine-computed audience, tombstones and
`bootstrap`; `schedule`, `job`, `chunk` and rehearsal; personas; `init`,
`dev`, `check`, `doctor`, `run`, `test`, `why`, `trace`, `guide`; H0
`deploy`, `rollback`, `secret`; channels; assets; the word-prefix index.

**Flip 1 — certify authorization, meter resources** (LLP 2000.000 §6). The
certificate keeps every read site's shape, uniformity, completeness class
and prediction eligibility, and stops pricing bytes and steps. A
deterministic meter charges examined rows, index entries, rule probes,
steps, heap, output and rows written as the program runs, on the server and
in the client interpreter alike. A query cut by the meter returns `capped`
with no continuation past the cut, the same observable outcome as a static
ceiling cut today; a mutation aborts with `E_BOUND` naming actual work; a
job is chunked. `check --cost` prints the structural cost class; `test`
prints measured meters on the hub fixture.

**Flip 2 — the viewer's partition is the unit of sync** (LLP 2000.000 §7).
`sync to <audience> last N by <index>` on a table makes the engine maintain,
per principal, the rows that principal may read, as a change log with a
horizon; a table without the word is online-only, and `check` says which
rule term prevented inversion. The client holds a replica of its partitions,
one watermark each, a durable outbox with client-minted ids, and the
interpreter; queries run locally and are `complete` inside the horizon.
Revocation is a scope tombstone; `until-revoked` and `delivered-history`
survive as the client's leave policy. Two client tiers — online-only
without a store, local-first with one — share one language and one server.

**The vocabulary is fixed before the mechanism** (LLP 2000.000 §8):

```ts
type Read<T> = { data: T; complete: boolean; fresh: boolean; since?: number; next?: Cursor }
            | { loading: true } | { denied: Refusal };
row.pending: boolean;
type Write = { state: "pending" } | { state: "sent"; seq: number } | { state: "failed"; why: Refusal };
type Link = "online" | "offline" | "signed-out";
```

A screen that needs a word not on that card is a defect in the mechanism,
not a gap in the card.

**The hub comes first** (LLP 2000.000 §11): the Clique generator's `u0001`
with 1,000 memberships, `u0500` with 500 follows, and about 100,000
messages are the first fixture; day-two changes are designed before the
day-one screen; the native client is in slice one; physical floors are
measured before targets; the simulator is the primary harness.

/bin/bash -lc 'timeout 10s cat snapback4/crates/snapback4/src/serve_maintenance.rs' in /home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b17-mig
