        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        for n in 0..count {
            let id = format!("r{n:04}");
            let data = canonical_json(&crate::value::object([
                ("id", Value::Id(id.clone())), ("payload", Value::String("x".repeat(payload))),
            ]));
            tx.tx.execute("INSERT INTO r(t,id,data) VALUES(1,?1,?2)", params![id, data]).unwrap();
        }
        tx.commit().unwrap();
        store
    }

    #[test]
    fn callback_keeps_the_whole_fetched_page_reserved() {
        let mut store = Store::memory().unwrap();
        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        let mut serialized_bytes = 0;
        for n in 0..20 {
            let id = format!("r{n:04}");
            let data = canonical_json(&crate::value::object([
                ("id", Value::Id(id.clone())), ("payload", Value::String("x".repeat(1024))),
            ]));
            serialized_bytes += (id.len() + data.len()) as u64;
            tx.tx.execute("INSERT INTO r(t,id,data) VALUES(1,?1,?2)", params![id, data]).unwrap();
        }
        let mut calls = 0;
        let mut first_heap = None;
        walk_metered(&tx, 1, adoption::Work::DECODE, None, |_, row, meter| {
            let mut decoder = Meter::new(Ceilings::unbounded(), Cut::Abort);
            adoption::charge(&mut decoder, adoption::decode_bytes(&canonical_json(&row)))?;
            let decode = decoder.used.heap_bytes;
            // Independent lower bound: Rust-owned images and both native
            // payload copies coexist with decode. This excludes headers/slots,
            // so it does not just repeat the walker's allocation formula.
            assert!(meter.used.heap_bytes >= 3 * serialized_bytes + decode,
                "Rust and native page copies must coexist with decoder scratch: {:?}", meter.used);
            let expected = first_heap.get_or_insert(meter.used.heap_bytes);
            assert_eq!(meter.used.heap_bytes, *expected, "earlier rows release only their own scratch");
            assert_eq!(meter.used.examined, 20 + calls + 1, "all admission decodes plus callback decodes are charged");
            calls += 1;
            Ok(())
        }).unwrap();
        assert_eq!(calls, 20);
        tx.rollback().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn heap_retries_keep_admission_examinations_at_the_callback_boundary() {
        let mut store = fixture(5, 1280 << 10);
        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        let work = adoption::Work { examined: 2, steps: 1, index_entries: 1 };
        let scratch = |row: &Value| adoption::contribution_bytes(row, &crate::schema::public_table(Default::default(), Default::default()));
        let mut observed = Vec::new();
        walk_metered(&tx, 1, work, Some(&scratch), |_, row, meter| {
            observed.push(meter.used.examined);
            assert_eq!((meter.used.steps, meter.used.index_entries), (0, 0), "rejected attempts perform no contribution work");
            meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
            meter.step(1)?;
            adoption::charge(meter, scratch(&row))?;
            meter.charge(MeterKind::IndexEntries, 1)?;
            assert!(meter.heap_peak <= Ceilings::job().heap_bytes);
            Ok(())
        }).unwrap();
        // Four two-image attempts each decode one row before the heap check
        // asks for a singleton. Its admission and callback decode add two.
        // The last source is already a singleton and needs no rejected attempt.
        assert_eq!(observed, [3, 3, 3, 3, 2]);
        tx.rollback().unwrap();
    }

    #[test]
    fn every_cumulative_budget_fixes_the_page_before_any_callback() {
        for (work, sizes) in [
            (adoption::Work { examined: 64, steps: 63, index_entries: 63 }, vec![252, 4]),
            (adoption::Work { examined: 2, steps: 5040, index_entries: 1 }, vec![198, 58]),
            (adoption::Work { examined: 1, steps: 0, index_entries: 400 }, vec![40, 40, 40, 40, 40, 40, 16]),
        ] {
            let mut store = fixture(256, 0);
            let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
            let (mut page, mut offset, mut calls) = (0, 0u64, 0);
            walk_metered(&tx, 1, work, None, |_, _, meter| {
                assert_eq!(meter.used.examined, sizes[page] + offset * work.examined + 1,
                    "the entire admission pass and every earlier callback remain charged");
                assert_eq!(meter.used.steps, offset * work.steps);
                assert_eq!(meter.used.index_entries, offset * work.index_entries);
                meter.charge(MeterKind::Examined, work.examined - 1)?;
                meter.step(work.steps)?;
                meter.charge(MeterKind::IndexEntries, work.index_entries)?;
                calls += 1;
                offset += 1;
                if offset == sizes[page] { page += 1; offset = 0; }
                Ok(())
            }).unwrap();
            assert_eq!(calls, 256);
            assert_eq!(page, sizes.len());
            tx.rollback().unwrap();
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn only_non_fitting_singletons_refuse_before_callbacks() {
        for (work, kind) in [
            (adoption::Work { examined: 16_384, steps: 0, index_entries: 0 }, MeterKind::Examined),
            (adoption::Work { examined: 1, steps: 1_000_001, index_entries: 0 }, MeterKind::Steps),
            (adoption::Work { examined: 1, steps: 0, index_entries: 16_385 }, MeterKind::IndexEntries),
        ] {
            for count in [0, 1] {
                let mut store = fixture(count, 0);
                let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
                let mut calls = 0;
                let result = walk_metered(&tx, 1, work, None, |_, _, _| { calls += 1; Ok(()) });
                assert_eq!(calls, 0, "no callback can start with an impossible page budget");
                if count == 0 { result.unwrap(); }
                else { assert!(matches!(result, Err(RuntimeError::Bound { kind: got, .. }) if got == kind), "{result:?}"); }
                tx.rollback().unwrap();
            }
        }
    }
}
//! A bounded serialized read-ahead buffer used only inside server activation.
//! Logical callers still fetch and price exactly one row at a time.
// @ref LLP 3000.002#implementation-follow-up — separate bounded raw workspace preserves logical admission.
use super::*;
use crate::{
    meter::{Ceilings, Cut, Meter},
    rows::word_heap as heap,
};
use std::{cell::RefCell, collections::VecDeque};

pub(super) type Buffer = RefCell<Option<Page>>;

pub(super) struct Page {
    table: i64,
    index: i64,
    lo: Vec<u8>,
    hi: Vec<u8>,
    rows: VecDeque<(String, Vec<u8>)>,
    /// Retain the admission for the complete buffer, including consumed slots.
    _meter: Meter,
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod tests {
    use super::*;
    use crate::{engine::InternalLedger, rows::Rows, value::object};

    fn fixture() -> (Store, Schema) {
        let bound = snapback4_lang::compile(&[("schema.q".into(), "table entries:\n  n: int\n  text: text <=200000\n  public\n  online only\nquery entries():\n  return entries first 20 by .n\n".into())]);
        assert!(bound.diagnostics.is_empty(), "{:?}", bound.diagnostics);
        let schema: Schema =
            serde_json::from_str(&serde_json::to_string(&bound.schema).unwrap()).unwrap();
        let mut store = Store::memory().unwrap();
        store.install(&schema).unwrap();
        let tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        for n in 0..96 {
            let row = object([
                ("id", Value::Id(format!("r{n:03}"))),
                ("n", Value::Int(n)),
                (
                    "text",
                    Value::String("x".repeat(if n == 40 { 150_000 } else { 100 })),
                ),
            ]);
            tx.put("entries", &schema.tables["entries"], &row, None)
                .unwrap();
        }
        tx.commit().unwrap();
        (store, schema)
    }

    #[test]
    fn activation_read_ahead_preserves_rows_cursors_and_every_logical_charge() {
        let (mut store, schema) = fixture();
        let index = schema.tables["entries"]
            .indexes
            .iter()
            .find(|(_, i)| i.columns().first().is_some_and(|c| c == "n"))
            .unwrap()
            .0;
        let mut tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        let mut bounds = Bounds::default();
        for n in 0..=96 {
            tx.activation_scan = None;
            let mut slow = Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort);
            let a = InternalLedger::with_meter(&mut slow, |meter, scope| {
                Rows::scan_metered(
                    &tx,
                    "entries",
                    index,
                    &[],
                    &bounds,
                    Dir::Asc,
                    1,
                    scope,
                    meter,
                )
            })
            .unwrap();
            tx.activation_scan = Some(Default::default());
            // Fill/reuse the page by reading the predecessor first, where there is one.
            if n > 0 {
                let before = Bounds {
                    after: Some(vec![Value::Int(n - 2), Value::Id(format!("r{:03}", n - 2))]),
                    ..Default::default()
                };
                let mut ignored = Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort);
                InternalLedger::with_meter(&mut ignored, |meter, scope| {
                    Rows::scan_metered(
                        &tx,
                        "entries",
                        index,
                        &[],
                        &before,
                        Dir::Asc,
                        1,
                        scope,
                        meter,
                    )
                })
                .unwrap();
            }
            let mut fast = Meter::new(Ceilings::job(), Cut::Abort);
            let b = InternalLedger::with_meter(&mut fast, |meter, scope| {
                Rows::scan_metered(
                    &tx,
                    "entries",
                    index,
                    &[],
                    &bounds,
                    Dir::Asc,
                    1,
                    scope,
                    meter,
                )
            })
            .unwrap();
            assert_eq!(a, b, "row {n}");
            assert_eq!(slow.used, fast.used, "meter {n}");
            if let Some((_, key)) = a.last() {
                bounds.after = crate::key::decode(key);
            }
        }
    }

    #[test]
    fn activation_read_ahead_is_invalidated_by_writes_and_raw_access() {
        let (mut store, schema) = fixture();
        let mut tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        tx.activation_scan = Some(Default::default());
        let t = tx.num("entries").unwrap();
        let ti = tx.num("entries.byId").unwrap();
        assert!(
            tx.activation_head(t, ti, &[], &[255])
                .unwrap()
                .flatten()
                .is_some()
        );
        let mut row = tx.get("entries", "r001").unwrap().unwrap();
        let old = row.clone();
        if let Value::Row(fields) = &mut row {
            fields.insert("text".into(), Value::String("changed".into()));
        }
        tx.put("entries", &schema.tables["entries"], &row, Some(&old))
            .unwrap();
        assert!(tx.activation_scan.as_ref().unwrap().borrow().is_none());
        tx.activation_head(t, ti, &[], &[255]).unwrap();
        let _ = tx.conn();
        assert!(tx.activation_scan.as_ref().unwrap().borrow().is_none());
        tx.activation_head(t, ti, &[], &[255]).unwrap();
        tx.delete("entries", &schema.tables["entries"], &row)
            .unwrap();
        assert!(tx.activation_scan.as_ref().unwrap().borrow().is_none());
    }

    #[test]
    fn raw_projection_and_savepoint_rollback_discard_buffered_images() {
        let (mut store, schema) = fixture();
        let mut tx = store.transaction().unwrap();
        tx.activation_scan = Some(Default::default());
        let t = tx.num("entries").unwrap();
        let ti = tx.num("entries.byId").unwrap();
        let old = tx.get("entries", "r001").unwrap().unwrap();
        let mut changed = old.clone();
        if let Value::Row(fields) = &mut changed {
            fields.insert("text".into(), Value::String("temporary".into()));
        }
        tx.savepoint("before_projection").unwrap();
        tx.activation_head(t, ti, &[], &[255]).unwrap();
        // The same getter used by activation's raw projection/staging SQL.
        tx.conn().execute("UPDATE r SET data=?1 WHERE t=?2 AND id='r001'",
            params![canonical_json(&changed), t]).unwrap();
        assert!(tx.activation_scan.as_ref().unwrap().borrow().is_none());
        // Cache the changed r001 behind r000, then roll the physical write back.
        tx.activation_head(t, ti, &[], &[255]).unwrap();
        assert!(tx.activation_scan.as_ref().unwrap().borrow().is_some());
        tx.rollback_to("before_projection").unwrap();
        assert!(tx.activation_scan.as_ref().unwrap().borrow().is_none());
        let key = crate::rows::index_key(&schema.tables["entries"].indexes["byId"], &old, "r001");
        let (data, _) = tx.activation_head(t, ti, &key, &[255]).unwrap().unwrap().unwrap();
        assert_eq!(serde_json::from_str::<Value>(&data).unwrap(), old);
    }
}

impl Tx<'_> {
    pub(super) fn clear_activation_scan(&self) {
        if let Some(buffer) = &self.activation_scan {
            buffer.borrow_mut().take();
        }
    }

    /// None means use the ordinary adapter; Some(None) proves an empty range.
    /// No Value is decoded by read-ahead, so malformed/unvisited payloads do not
    /// change a caller's result or refusal. A too-wide first row uses the old path.
    pub(super) fn activation_head(
        &self,
        t: i64,
        ti: i64,
        lo: &[u8],
        hi: &[u8],
    ) -> Result<Option<Option<(String, Vec<u8>)>>, RuntimeError> {
        let Some(buffer) = &self.activation_scan else {
            return Ok(None);
        };
        let mut held = buffer.borrow_mut();
        if let Some(page) = held.as_mut() {
            if page.table == t && page.index == ti && page.hi == hi && lo >= page.lo.as_slice() {
                while page
                    .rows
                    .front()
                    .is_some_and(|(_, key)| key.as_slice() < lo)
                {
                    page.rows.pop_front();
                }
                if let Some(row) = page.rows.pop_front() {
                    // Only forward cursors may reuse the unread tail.
                    page.lo = crate::key::upper_bound(&row.1);
                    return Ok(Some(Some(row)));
                }
            }
        }
        held.take();
        const PAGE: usize = 32;
        const BYTES: u64 = 128 * 1024;
        let mut meter = Meter::new(
            Ceilings {
                heap_bytes: BYTES,
                ..Ceilings::job()
            },
            Cut::Abort,
        );
        meter.at("adopt serialized read-ahead");
        let fixed = heap::slots::<(String, Vec<u8>)>(PAGE)
            + heap::allocation(lo.len())
            + heap::allocation(hi.len())
            // upper_bound clones then appends: reserve the old cursor, clone,
            // and the Vec growth replacement together, including capacity.
            + 4 * heap::allocation(2 * crate::rows::MAX_INDEX_KEY_BYTES + 1)
            + 2 * self.page_size;
        // An unusually large SQLite page can simply disable this optimization.
        if !meter.room(crate::error::MeterKind::HeapBytes, fixed) {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        meter.heap(fixed)?;
        let mut count = 0;
        {
            let mut statement = self.tx.prepare_cached("SELECT octet_length(r.data), length(i.k) FROM i JOIN r ON r.t = ?1 AND r.id = i.id WHERE i.ti = ?2 AND i.k >= ?3 AND i.k < ?4 ORDER BY i.k LIMIT 32")?;
            let mut rows = statement.query(params![t, ti, lo, hi])?;
            while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
                let bytes = 3
                    * (heap::allocation(row.get::<_, i64>(0)? as usize)
                        + heap::allocation(row.get::<_, i64>(1)? as usize))
                    + 64;
                if !meter.room(crate::error::MeterKind::HeapBytes, bytes) {
                    break;
                }
                meter.heap(bytes)?;
                meter.charge(crate::error::MeterKind::Examined, 1)?;
                count += 1;
            }
        }
        if count == 0 {
            return Ok(None);
        }
        let mut page = Page {
            table: t,
            index: ti,
            lo: lo.to_vec(),
            hi: hi.to_vec(),
            rows: VecDeque::with_capacity(PAGE),
            _meter: meter,
        };
        {
            let mut statement = self.tx.prepare_cached(scan_sql(Dir::Asc))?;
            let mut rows = statement.query(params![t, ti, lo, hi, count])?;
            while let Some(row) = rows.next()? {
                page.rows.push_back((row.get(0)?, row.get(1)?));
            }
        }
        let first = page.rows.pop_front();
        if let Some((_, key)) = &first {
            page.lo = crate::key::upper_bound(key);
        }
        *held = Some(page);
        Ok(Some(first))
    }
}

fn report(verb: &str, result: Result<(), String>) -> i32 {
    // @ref LLP 3000#contended-read-serving — release completion owns no engine/lease; bound the final diagnostic drain.
    // The background writer must get a chance to emit adoption estimates before
    // this short-lived command exits. Broken/stalled output cannot hold exit.
    let _ = snapback4_core::diagnostics::drain(std::time::Duration::from_secs(3));
    match result {
        Ok(()) => 0,
        Err(error) => {
            eprintln!("{verb}: {error}");
            1
        }
    }
}

//! Immutable source releases with a database-authoritative activation pointer.
use super::*;
use crate::store_owner::Owner;
use std::path::{Path, PathBuf};
#[path = "staging.rs"]
mod staging;
struct Stage(PathBuf);
impl Drop for Stage {fn drop(&mut self){let _=std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0);}}

fn directory(options: &Options) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    options
        .positionals
        .first()
        .map(PathBuf::from)
        .ok_or_else(|| "a deployment directory is required".into())
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000#5.1 — deployment aliases share ownership, control and worker paths.
fn canonical_directory(options: &Options) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    let requested = directory(options)?;
    if !requested.exists() {
        snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(&requested).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    }
    let dir = requested.canonicalize().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    snapback4_core::private_fs::directory(&dir).map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    Ok(dir)
}

// @ref LLP 3000.000.000.000.000#8 — validate before any writable ownership or command lock.
pub(crate) fn existing_deployment(requested: &Path) -> Result<PathBuf, String> {
    let missing = || format!("no current release in {}; run `snapback4 deploy {}` first", requested.display(), requested.display());
    if !requested.join("store.sqlite").is_file() { return Err(missing()); }
    let dir = requested.canonicalize().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    inspect_current(&dir)?;
    Ok(dir)
}

// SQLite READONLY can create WAL sidecars. A stopped store's existing owner
// lock makes immutable inspection safe; a live host supplies its own status.
fn inspect_current(dir: &Path) -> Result<u64, String> {
    use rusqlite::{Connection, OpenFlags, OptionalExtension};
    let database = dir.join("store.sqlite").canonicalize().map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
    let missing = || format!("no current release in {}; run `snapback4 deploy {}` first", dir.display(), dir.display());
    let owner = match snapback4_core::private_fs::auxiliary_file(&database,
        &snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_path(&database), false, 0) {
        Ok(owner) => owner,
        Err(error) if error.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => {
            // Relocated/legacy deployments may not yet have a sidecar beside
            // the resolved DB. Establish a complete current source first; only
            // a known deployment may let SQLite create its ordinary WAL files.
            return pointer_current(dir, &database);
        },
        Err(error) => return Err(format!("{}; existing ownership sidecar unavailable: {error}", missing())),
    };
    match owner.try_lock() {
        Ok(()) => {},
        Err(std::fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) => {
            match crate::release_control::request(dir, crate::release_control::Command::Status {after:0, items_after:None, event:None}) {
                Ok(status) => return status["release"].as_u64().filter(|n|*n>0).ok_or_else(missing),
                Err(error) => {
                    // A killed host's watchdogs retain ownership during their
                    // bounded cleanup. Preserve serve's existing restart wait.
                    if !crate::store_owner::stopped_host(&database) {
                        // A second source directory may alias the same DB. Its
                        // source cannot control this host, but its token still
                        // belongs to the resolved database. Establish current
                        // source before permitting ordinary read-only WAL work.
                        return pointer_current(dir, &database).map_err(|_| format!("{}; {error}",missing()));
                    }
                    let deadline=std::time::Instant::now()+std::time::Duration::from_secs(5);
                    loop {
                        match owner.try_lock() {
                            Ok(()) => break,
                            Err(std::fs::TryLockError::WouldBlock) if std::time::Instant::now()<deadline => std::thread::sleep(std::time::Duration::from_millis(25)),
                            _ => return Err(format!("{}; {error}",missing())),
                        }
                    }
                }
            }
        },
        Err(error) => return Err(error.to_string()),
    }
    if !snapback4_core::private_fs::owner_is_named(&database, &owner) {
        return Err("store ownership changed during release inspection; retry".into());
    }
    #[cfg(unix)]
    let bytes = { use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt; database.as_os_str().as_bytes() };
    #[cfg(not(unix))]
    let bytes = database.to_str().ok_or("invalid store path")?.as_bytes();
    let mut uri = String::from("file:");
    for byte in bytes {
        if byte.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || b"/._-".contains(byte) { uri.push(*byte as char); }
        else { uri.push_str(&format!("%{byte:02X}")); }
    }
    let mut wal = database.as_os_str().to_os_string(); wal.push("-wal"); let wal = PathBuf::from(wal);
    let mut shm = database.as_os_str().to_os_string(); shm.push("-shm"); let shm = PathBuf::from(shm);
    let has_wal = match std::fs::metadata(&wal) {
        Ok(meta) => meta.len() > 0,
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => false,
        Err(e) => return Err(e.to_string()),
    };
    if has_wal && !shm.is_file() { return Err("store has a WAL without its shared-memory sidecar; run deploy on this stopped deployment to recover it before inspection".into()); }
    // Immutable SQLite omits WAL reads: use it only for the checkpointed main
    // image. Existing WAL+SHM can be read normally under the same exclusion.
    uri.push_str(if has_wal { "?mode=ro" } else { "?mode=ro&immutable=1" });
    let conn = Connection::open_with_flags(uri, OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_READ_ONLY | OpenFlags::SQLITE_OPEN_URI).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
    let release: Option<String> = conn.query_row("SELECT value FROM _meta WHERE key='release'", [], |row|row.get(0)).optional().map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
    let release = match release {
        Some(value) => value,
        None => std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("current")).map_err(|_| missing())?,
    };
    release.trim().parse::<u64>().ok().filter(|n|*n>0).ok_or_else(missing)
}

fn pointer_current(dir: &Path, database: &Path) -> Result<u64, String> {
    let missing = || format!("no current release in {}; deploy first", dir.display());
    let pointer = std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("current")).map_err(|_| missing())?;
    let pointer = pointer.trim().parse::<u64>().ok().filter(|n|*n>0).ok_or_else(missing)?;
    bound_at(dir.join("releases").join(pointer.to_string()))?;
    let store = snapback4_core::Store::open_read_only(database).map_err(|e|e.to_string())?;
    match store.meta("release").map_err(|e|e.to_string())? {
        Some(value) => value.parse::<u64>().ok().filter(|n|*n>0).ok_or_else(missing),
        None => Ok(pointer),
    }
}

/// `dev` and `serve` hold the store-owner lock for their lifetime. Release
/// commands route to the admitted server when it owns this deployment.
pub(crate) fn deployment_lock(dir: &Path) -> Result<Owner, String> {
    crate::store_owner::command(&dir.join("store.sqlite"))
}
fn current(dir: &Path, owner: &Owner) -> Result<Option<u64>, String> {
    let database = dir.join("store.sqlite");
    if database.exists() {
        let store = owner
            .open_store(std::time::Duration::from_secs(5))
            .map_err(|e| e.to_string())?;
        if let Some(release) = store.meta("release").map_err(|e| e.to_string())? {
            return release
                .parse()
                .map(Some)
                .map_err(|_| "invalid release identity in store".into());
        }
    }
    // Compatibility with deployments made before the database owned this
    // pointer. The next activation records it transactionally.
    match std::fs::read_to_string(dir.join("current")) {
        Ok(text) => text
            .trim()
            .parse()
            .map(Some)
            .map_err(|_| "invalid current release file".into()),
        Err(e) if e.kind() == std::io::ErrorKind::NotFound => Ok(None),
        Err(e) => Err(format!("cannot read current release: {e}")),
    }
}

/// The retirement phase shared by activation and its read-only occupancy
/// preview. Selection and the predecessor deadline predicate live here once;
/// checking a candidate must not count a row this phase would remove.
pub(crate) struct Retirement<'a> {
    affected: Vec<(String, &'a Table)>,
    now: i64,
}

impl<'a> Retirement<'a> {
    pub(crate) fn new(next: &Schema, previous: &'a Schema, now: i64) -> Self {
        let affected = next
            .through_order()
            .into_iter()
            .filter_map(|name| {
                let next = &next.tables[&name];
                let old = previous.table(&name)?;
                Self::changes_lifetime(next,old).then_some((name, old))
            })
            .collect();
        Self { affected, now }
    }

    fn changes_lifetime(next:&Table,old:&Table) -> bool {
        next.through != old.through || next.through.is_some() && (next.expire != old.expire || next.expire.as_ref().is_some_and(|field|old.defaults.get(field)!=next.defaults.get(field)))
    }

    pub(crate) fn retires_image(next:&Table,old:&Table,row:&Value,now:i64) -> bool {
        (next.through!=old.through || next.expire!=old.expire || old.expire.as_ref().is_some_and(|field|old.defaults.get(field)!=next.defaults.get(field))) && old.expired(row,now)
    }

    pub(crate) fn affects(&self, name: &str) -> bool {
        self.affected.iter().any(|(table, _)| table == name)
    }

    pub(crate) fn retires(&self, name: &str, row: &Value) -> bool {
        self.affected
            .iter()
            .find(|(table, _)| table == name)
            .is_some_and(|(_, old)| old.expired(row, self.now))
    }
}

/// Capture barrier for an authoritative adapter's uncommitted generation.
pub fn activate(
    tx: &dyn Rows,
    next: &Schema,
    previous: Option<&Schema>,
    now: i64,
) -> Result<std::collections::BTreeMap<String, u64>, RuntimeError> {
    activate_retained(tx, next, previous, now, &Default::default())
}

- **[P1] Restored narrowed rows can lose saved reference lifetimes.** [backfills.rs:244](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b17-mig/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/store/backfills.rs:244) chooses input binding types from the table-wide predecessor, ignoring the restored row’s historical definition. Reproduce with a reference-bearing v1 row, a v2 that narrows the row and changes its reference column to generic `id`, then a widening v3 backfill consuming that input as `id`. No private reference binding is captured; restoration cleanup removes the original column binding. Deleting/reusing the parent and re-entering v3 can then read the replacement parent. Capture bindings from each restored row’s actual source definition before consuming its original ledger.

- **[P1] Historical lifetime-output protection misses narrowed provenance.** [backfills.rs:63](/home/ccheever/projects/sb4-b17-mig/snapback4/crates/snapback4-core/src/store/backfills.rs:63) checks only the table-wide source. A v1 row archived by narrowing retains its original expiry definition. If v2 removes that expiry rule, a widening v3 can backfill the original expiry column because the table-wide predecessor no longer marks it protected. The restored row’s historical lifetime can therefore be rewritten despite the RFC’s explicit prohibition. Check output ownership against restored narrowed definitions before evaluating any patch; cover expiry, opening boundaries, captured fields, and historical reference types.
